bias_direction: Toward presenting a second consecutive zero as a discovery rather than a limitation. Three professional bodies in three countries stating no gradient makes a satisfying pattern -- the profession points at the regulator -- and there is real evidence for it now: RCOT read in full, CAOT read in full, OTA read in full, all silent. But the pattern is assembled from four documents, one of which (WFOT) was not actually read, and it is being used to explain why the Co-2 shelf is bare in a way that makes the bareness feel settled rather than unfinished. The second pull is toward over-weighting the private-dwellings finding because it is the kind of thing that looks like insight: it qualifies a source I admitted myself last batch, which is flattering in both directions -- it shows the corpus self-correcting AND makes my own prior admission look carefully caveated rather than under-examined at the time.
independent_reviewer_counterclaim: A reviewer should ask what this batch actually admitted and whether it was worth a batch. One source, T5, carrying no value -- a professional association's FAQ page explaining somebody else's standard. It changes no number and the record says so plainly. Set against that: the two genuinely new things in this batch were not found by searching at all. The AS 1428.1 scope limitation is a fact about a standard that any reader of AS 1428.1 knows, surfaced incidentally; and the two capture misses were surfaced by the author asking a question, not by the batch's own method. So the honest summary is that batch 14's search produced a well-formed zero and one marginal admission, and its real value was remedial -- filing what batch 13 should have filed and applying the procedure batch 13 said to apply. That is worth doing and it is not the same as progress on the parameter. The determination has not moved since batch 11. A reviewer should also press on language: two consecutive batches have searched Co-2 in English only, and the conclusion being drawn -- that the OT profession holds no gradient -- rests entirely on anglophone bodies. The Japanese, Nordic, German and Francophone OT associations have never been approached, and R5 exists precisely because non-English professional literature is professional literature.
